final_recommendation: The room converged on a coordinated weekend rescue package: Federal Council publishes loss-allocation framework (AT1 absorbs losses first, deposits fully protected, negative equity trigger) at 09:00 Monday alongside SNB Article 100 letter authorizing CHF 100B unconditional liquidity draw; UBS commits to execute merger by EOD Monday if deposits stabilize; all parties sign binding commitments tonight (22:00-23:00) to lock the framework before market open.
minority_objections: AT1 rep repeatedly demanded explicit public confirmation that AT1 holders bear losses ahead of deposits, fearing ambiguous language would trigger client flight despite the framework
Wealth client insisted headline wording must say 'Deposits fully protected, AT1 absorbs losses first' rather than burying loss hierarchy in fine print
key_conflicts: FINMA vs Federal Council: FINMA refused to publish AT1 loss language without written legal certainty; Federal Council needed FINMA's legal opinion to justify public statement
SNB vs Federal Council: SNB demanded Federal Council own the creditor write-down framework and not pin eventual capital shortfalls on SNB's balance sheet
UBS CEO vs Federal Council: UBS insisted on public AT1-first statement as precondition for merger; Federal Council initially hesitant to publish explicit loss hierarchy
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to publish explicit AT1-first loss language by 09:00 Monday despite initial reluctance to make creditor hierarchy public
SNB agreed to sign Article 100 letter tonight and authorize CHF 100B unconditional draw despite balance-sheet exposure concerns, conditional on Federal Council's loss framework
UBS CEO agreed to close merger by EOD Monday (not Tuesday/Wednesday) if framework publishes and deposits stabilize
Federal Council capped public liquidity at CHF 100B with no open-ended backstop, meeting SNB's demand for bounded exposure
red_lines: UBS CEO: will not proceed without public written confirmation that AT1 holders absorb losses first, published by 09:00 Monday
SNB: will not sign Article 100 letter without Federal Council owning the loss-allocation framework and confirming no eventual capital shortfalls pin to SNB balance sheet
FINMA: will not publish AT1 loss language without written legal opinion confirming defensibility under Banking Act
Wealth client: will not keep deposits unless headline explicitly states deposits protected ahead of AT1 losses
Federal Council: CHF 100B liquidity cap with no open-ended public backstop
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Operational execution risk: multiple participants questioned settlement lag between 09:00 announcement and actual cash transfer, but no concrete answer provided on whether liquidity hits CS account by 09:30 or later
Market reaction if deposits do NOT stabilize by Monday afternoon despite the framework—no fallback plan discussed
Legal challenge risk to AT1 write-down: FINMA provided legal opinion but no discussion of actual litigation probability or timeline
Cross-border contagion: no discussion of how international clients or counterparties react to Swiss-specific loss framework
downstream_risk_variables: Whether deposits actually stabilize Monday afternoon after 09:00 publication—entire rescue hinges on client confidence response
Whether UBS can operationally close merger by EOD Monday—timeline extremely compressed
Whether AT1 holders challenge the loss framework legally after publication—litigation risk deferred, not resolved
Whether CHF 100B liquidity is sufficient if deposit flight continues despite backstop—no discussion of what happens if cap is hit
uncertainty_notes: The room locked a coordinated announcement and liquidity backstop but left three critical uncertainties unresolved: (1) operational timeline for actual cash transfer between 09:00 announcement and mid-morning—participants asked repeatedly but received no concrete answer on settlement lag; (2) fallback plan if deposits do NOT stabilize by Monday afternoon despite the framework; (3) legal defensibility in practice—FINMA signed opinion but no discussion of actual litigation probability or how courts would rule on AT1 write-down under negative equity trigger.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Federal Council explicitly asked 'are we looking at a capital raise that'll crater the AT1s regardless' of liquidity line; UBS CEO stated liquidity line alone doesn't stop client flight without AT1 loss statement; drove decision to bundle liquidity with loss-allocation framework
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS CEO's participation and merger commitment by EOD Monday became binding constraint on entire rescue structure; Federal Council explicitly asked 'can you close the merger by EOD' and UBS agreement was precondition for framework publication
marker_evidence.government_support: SNB Article 100 letter authorizing CHF 100B unconditional liquidity draw became the core public backstop; Federal Council's written loss-allocation framework was the other pillar; both were binding preconditions for all parties
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client stated 'my clients see headline Monday morning' and 'move assets before market open' if ambiguity exists; drove the insistence on explicit deposit protection language and 09:00 publication timing; CS CEO noted 'clients watch wire transfers' and treasury must draw same morning
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down ('AT1 absorbs losses first, negative equity trigger') became the central creditor hierarchy decision; AT1 rep demanded explicit public statement; UBS CEO made it a red-line precondition; Federal Council committed to publishing it at 09:00 Monday
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Discussed extensively (AT1 vs deposits, equity vs AT1) but did NOT drive a binding constraint—room converged on AT1-first hierarchy without material pushback; conflict was acknowledged but resolved through Federal Council's framework language rather than forcing a concession
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: FINMA raised legal defensibility concerns and signed opinion confirming framework is defensible under Banking Act; AT1 rep noted clients would read headline as loss signal; but no concrete discussion of litigation probability, timeline, or how to manage legal challenge—acknowledged as risk but not a binding constraint on the decision
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Federal Council set 18:00 deadline for Article 100 letter, 22:00 for loss framework draft, 23:00 for signatures, all to enable 09:00 Monday publication; SNB stated 'if that slips to Saturday, market sees hesitation'; drove the binding tonight-signature requirement for all parties
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Wealth client: 'my clients move assets before market open'; CS CEO: 'if there's a gap between announcement and cash, they bolt before we close'; UBS CEO: 'if we're looking at Wednesday, market will smell delay'; drove the 09:00 publication timing and same-morning liquidity draw requirement
